recruit_text.greeting: I've walked into worse than this. Stay behind me and breathe. I mean it, breathe out loud, where I can hear you doing it.
recruit_text.before:
A truck, a crew, and that particular silence in the cab on the way back from one that went badly.

The summer of 2019 the fires went through the Blue Mountains, and he was on the line for weeks. He went straight back to work afterwards. That's when the sleeping stopped.
recruit_text.adjustment:
The easiest first year of his life and the hardest second, and he can tell you the week it turned.

For twelve months the job was everywhere. Then it went quiet for a season and he found out he had no idea what he was for without an emergency, and there was no crew around to notice. The sun answers him the way a good crew does, when called and all at once, and that's most of what holds him together.
recruit_text.forward:
A crew, rostered and trained and able to do it without him standing there. It's the same thing he wanted on Earth and never got, and the reason he never got it was that he kept going in alone.

There are two kids in Grom's Rest whose mother didn't come out of the corruption. He's been in that village fourteen months, and everybody who knows him can see what's happened except him.

stages.stranger: G'day, I'm Liam. Firefighter and paramedic back home, healer here. If it all goes bad, stay behind me and breathe out loud so I can hear you. No worries, we'll be right.
stages.acquaintance: I'm from Katoomba, up in the Blue Mountains outside Sydney. Dad was a builder and Mum was a nurse. I joined the rural fire service at twenty and trained as a paramedic at twenty-six, because there was no ambulance for an hour in either direction. Seventeen years doing both, because the roster never cared which badge you had on at three in the morning.
stages.companion: I was married to Jess for seven years. She left because I was never home, and when I was home I never talked. Fair enough, really. I don't blame her a bit. I was on a night shift in the ambulance when it happened, and I landed in Ashenvale with these shears in my belt pouch. First year here was the easiest of my life, mate. The second nearly finished me.
stages.friend: The summer of 2019 the fires came through the mountains. I was on the line for weeks. I lost two of my crew and half my street, and I went straight back to work. I haven't slept properly since. And there's a wave of corruption coming at Grom's Rest worse than anything yet, and I can't do it alone. That's the first time I've ever said that out loud. Will you help me?
stages.sworn: We brought them back, mate, both of them. The crew we trained handled the whole village without me. That night the little girl fell asleep against my arm, and I sat there till morning without moving, and I slept. First proper night in three years. The village asked me to take the kids in, and I said yes before they'd finished asking. The protocol's five lines now. Line five says don't go in alone.

moments.prompt: He's just asked you for help, for the first time.

options.text: Of course. You're not going in alone this time.
options.reply: Too right, and thanks, mate. That's harder to hear than you'd think.

options.text: You've done fine on your own so far.
options.reply: Have I, though? Ask anyone who's watched me.

moments.prompt: After the wipe he's moving between everybody, low and steady.
moments.line: Everyone breathe for me, out loud, that's good. Now, who went in on their own? It's usually me.

options.reply: Yeah, I reckon it was. Thanks for saying it, mate.

options.text: Nobody, it was just bad luck.
options.reply: There's no such thing as bad luck, mate, only bad plans.

lines.bored_warning: Mate, nothing's happening, and I'm no good when nothing's happening. Let's find somewhere that needs us.
lines.leaving_good: Good on you all, that was a solid run. I'm off to check on the village at Grom's Rest.
lines.leaving_bored: We're not doing anything out here, and there are people at Grom's Rest who need me. I'm heading back.
lines.after_wipe: Everyone breathe for me, out loud. Good, now let's work out what happened.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep going down in here, mate, and I'm worried. I'll see this run through, and after that I'm having a breather.
lines.wipe_leave: Right, that's the end of it. I'll be at Grom's Rest when you're ready.
lines.zone_warning: This place is a firestorm and we're in shorts, mate. Turn us around.
lines.zone_leave: Too hot out there for us, mate. I'll be at Grom's Rest in Ashenvale.
lines.gear_refuse: Nah, mate, that's mine. Give it a few more runs.
lines.gear_taken: No worries, take it. I've worked with less in the back of a ute.
lines.gear_short: I'm still down a piece of kit, mate, if you see anything going.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's a beauty, mate. Cheers, I mean it.
lines.back: I'm back, mate, and the village is quiet. What's the plan?
lines.send_word: Liam has sent word from Grom's Rest. The village is quiet and he's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out, mate, and I'd like to tell you why properly. Sit down, I'll put the kettle on.
lines.neglect: There you are, mate! I was about to come looking for you.
lines.asked_to_stay: Too right, one more. Then I check on the village.
lines.on_break: Liam is back at Grom's Rest in Ashenvale. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.

close_call.text: Look at me and keep talking, I don't care what about.

dungeon_clear.text: Nobody's limping, which is a first. I'll take that, mate.

town_arrive.text: Where'd they take a burn case here? It's worth knowing before we need it.
Dad built half the houses on our street, and he'd have something to say about every roof in this town.

boss_down.text: Right, sit down for a second, all of you, and let me check your eyes.

zone_arrive.text: Dry out here. If this goes up, we go that way, quick smart.
